coverage.evidence: 'Lint is green with no error, and the two files over 400 lines are reported rather than ignored.' CI's verify passed on 43ebdce at https://github.com/AbuMahir980/mizaniya/actions/runs/38443383720/job/115455397499, and lint run directly reports '0 errors, 24 warnings'. The two files appear among the warnings with their real counts: home-screen.tsx 'File has too many lines (500)' and onboarding.tsx '(660)'. They are reported, not ignored.

'peer-ai doctor lists TS-08 as reporting only until ITEM-2, with the owner named and the two files named.' doctor prints: 'TS-08 only reports until ITEM-2 is done: Two files in apps/web are over the 400-line limit once the rule is actually applied: home-screen.tsx at 500 counted lines and onboarding.tsx at 660. Nothing else in source is over. ... (decided by Qudus Lawal)'. The reason also records why the limit was never reached before 2026-10-13, so a reader is not left to rediscover it.

'REACT-03's reason claimed TS-08 passes in source; that sentence is corrected.' The sentence 'TS-08's 400-line limit is NOT deferred; it passes in source, and its one finding is a test file the test override exempts' is gone from peer-ai.config.json, replaced by a dated correction naming why it was wrong: the deferral was silently replacing the enforced rule for every .tsx file. doctor prints the corrected text. The same false claim was also in docs/05-coding-standards.md, whose D1 row said 'Not yet - needs a line-count rule'; that row now names peer-ai/max-lines as REACT-03, its reporting status and the deferral, with a second row for the 400-line limit.

'A file over 400 lines is reported rather than silently passing.' It is, and the honest mechanics are worth stating: with TS-08 and REACT-03 both deferred, the threshold in force for a .tsx file is REACT-03's 150, so anything over 400 is necessarily reported too. What this change fixed is that the enforced setting is no longer dropped: with next.16 installed and before the TS-08 deferral was added, lint produced exactly two errors, 'File has too many lines (500). Maximum allowed is 400' and '(660)'. That is the rule biting, observed. When ITEM-2 ends the deferrals, both thresholds block instead of reporting, which is only true because the replacement bug is gone.

The check was seen failing before it was trusted, which is the whole point of this item. Under next.15 the 400-line rule reported nothing on any .tsx file, proven by its absence from lint output while two files were 500 and 660 lines. Under next.16 with nothing deferred it produced two errors. Under next.16 with the deferral it produces two warnings and no error. Three observed states, each matching what the configuration says it should be.

The defect was a rule that silently checked nothing, and what guards against its return is the fix in peer-ai-eslint-config itself, which leaves out a reporting-only setting wherever an enforced setting of the same ESLint rule covers the same files. Pinned exactly at 1.0.0-next.16, so the guard cannot regress without the lockfile changing. A project-level test asserting a lint rule fires already exists in this repository as the pattern - apps/web/src/architecture.test.ts does it for the boundary rules - and extending it to the length rules is recorded as worth doing when the deferrals end, since a test asserting a warning threshold would have to be rewritten at that point.

The edge case of this change is that the fix makes a false record visible rather than breaking code, and both places carrying the false record were corrected rather than one. The deferral was also written with the two file names and their line counts inside it, so when ITEM-2 reaches these files the next reader knows which two were over and by how much, without re-running anything.

summary: Pass, all four criteria on observed evidence. Three states of the same rule were seen: nothing reported under next.15 while two files stood at 500 and 660 lines, two errors under next.16 with nothing deferred, and two warnings with the deferral in place. The two records that said the rule was enforced and passing are corrected with their dates, and the deferral names both files, their counts, the owner and ITEM-2.
